barriers.description: Designers were unable to produce an initial functional prototype in the target magnesium alloy because the first prototype had to be manufactured in aluminum due to local access constraints. This limited their ability to test the design in the intended material early in the process.
barriers.justification: Requiring an aluminum prototype prevented designers from producing and evaluating solutions in the final material, hindering the 'produce design solutions' and 'evaluate designs' workloads (material-specific testing and iteration were deferred).
barriers.reference_excerpt: The first functional prototype is being manufactured in aluminum alloy, due to its ease of access in the local context. This prototype will be used to develop technical and usability tests. The resultant design will be prototyped in AZ31 magnesium alloy and the same tests mentioned will be applied.

barriers.description: Key manufacturing processes (surface treatments and powder metallurgy) were developed in parallel subprojects and had not been scaled for application, delaying their integration into the main design work. This separation constrained the team's ability to incorporate manufacturing solutions into the design on schedule.
barriers.justification: Because those processes were not yet scaled and integrated, the team could not finalize or test the magnesium prototype, hindering 'produce design solutions', 'integrate feedback & iteration', and coordination of the multidisciplinary team.
barriers.reference_excerpt: On the other hand, the processes for the treatment of the surfaces and the formation of pieces by powder metallurgy, were developed by materials engineers in parallel subprojects. The results of these subprojects will be integrated into the design process when said manufacturing processes are scaled for their application in the magnesium prototype.
